prompt.context: You have been asked to estimate the size of the acoustic piano market in the state of New Hampshire for 2012. Acoustic pianos include upright, grand, and baby grand pianos. Digital keyboards are out of scope.
prompt.question: What is the 2012 market size of acoustic pianos in the state of New Hampshire?

clarifying_info.q: What counts as an acoustic piano?
clarifying_info.a: Upright, grand, and baby grand pianos. Digital keyboards are out of scope.

clarifying_info.q: Should I include commercial/institutional buyers like concert halls or retail stores?
clarifying_info.a: It is safe to estimate the residential market only; you can ignore concert halls, inventory in retail stores, etc.

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of New Hampshire?
clarifying_info.a: Use your best estimate; the US population is about 300 million across 50 states, so average is 6 million per state. NH is one of the smallest states.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average household size?
clarifying_info.a: Use your best estimate; the US average is about 2.5 people per household.

framework: Define market scope: residential acoustic piano purchases (exclude concert halls, retail inventory, digital keyboards)
Estimate NH population using US total (300M / 50 states = 6M average; NH is a small state, estimate 1-2M)
Convert population to households using average household size (~2.5 people/HH)
Estimate % of households that own an acoustic piano (consider wealth, keyboard vs. acoustic mix, macro factors; likely under 5%)
Estimate average piano price (varies by type; upright < grand; estimate $5,000-$10,000)
Apply replacement rate: divide stock value by average piano lifespan (30-50 years) to get annual market size
Sanity-check and state final answer with confidence

questions.prompt: Walk through your approach and equation for estimating the market size.
questions.guidance: Candidate should articulate the equation: Market size = (Population of NH / Average Household Size) x % Owning Piano x Average Piano Price x Replacement Rate. They should identify each variable and explain the logic before calculating.

math.setup: Market size = (NH Population / HH size) x % owning piano x avg price x replacement rate
steps: NH population estimate: 1.5 million (small state reasoning)
Piano ownership rate: 5% → 600,000 x 5% = 30,000 piano-owning households

questions.prompt: What factors drive the % of households that own an acoustic piano in NH?
questions.guidance: Candidate should discuss: (1) average wealth of NH households (relatively higher than US average, supporting higher ownership), (2) mix of electric keyboards vs. acoustic pianos (many households may own a keyboard instead), (3) macroeconomic impacts — pianos are elastic/discretionary purchases. Reasonable range is 3-10%.

questions.prompt: How would changes to your assumptions affect your estimate?
questions.guidance: Excellent candidates should articulate directional sensitivity: e.g., if ownership rate is 3% instead of 5% the market is ~60% smaller (~$3.4M); if piano lifespan is 30 years instead of 40 years the market is ~33% larger (~$7.5M). Shows comfort with uncertainty and ability to frame a range.

recommendation: The 2012 residential acoustic piano market in New Hampshire is approximately $5.6 million per year, based on ~600,000 households, 5% ownership, $7,500 average price, and a 40-year replacement cycle.
risks: Ownership rate assumption is the most sensitive variable; range of 3-10% produces market estimates of ~$3.4M to ~$11.3M
Piano lifespan estimates (30-50 years) create a range of ~$4.5M to ~$7.5M
NH's above-average household wealth could push ownership and price assumptions higher
next_steps: Validate ownership rate assumption with consumer survey data or industry reports
Segment by piano type (upright vs. grand) if more precision is needed
Consider whether commercial/institutional channel adds meaningful additional volume
